title: Hunter's Chicken
subtitle: Chicken breasts wrapped in bacon with BBQ sauce and melted cheese
excerpt: Chicken breasts wrapped in smoked bacon, baked with a BBQ sauce glaze, and finished with melted cheddar. A British pub classic from the 1980s and 1990s and still one of the most-ordered dishes in casual dining.

recipe.sourceNotes: Hunter's chicken is a distinctly British casual-dining creation with no connection to the French or Italian chasseur or cacciatore dishes despite the name. It emerged in British pub and casual restaurant menus during the 1980s alongside the American-influenced BBQ sauce trend. The combination of bacon-wrapped chicken, BBQ sauce, and melted cheddar became a staple of chain restaurant menus and is widely reproduced at home.

content.text: This is a simple dish that is better when the chicken is browned in a pan before going into the oven. The pan-searing sets the bacon, starts the caramelisation, and gives the finished dish a better texture than going straight into the oven from raw. Use smoked streaky bacon for the best flavour. The BBQ sauce goes on halfway through so it caramelises rather than burning.

items.preparation: large, flattened slightly with a rolling pin

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Season the chicken breasts. Wrap each one tightly in 2 rashers of bacon, overlapping the rashers.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the bacon is beginning to colour.
Transfer the chicken to a baking dish. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove and spoon half the BBQ sauce over each chicken breast. Return to the oven for 8 minutes.
Add the remaining BBQ sauce and top each breast generously with grated cheddar. Return to the oven for 5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Serve with chips or mashed potato.
